competency_fulfillment.rationale: Thirteen of the fourteen samples ask on the face of the stem for an area in one of the two required units: seed 42 'A rectangle has sides 4 cm and 3 cm. What is its area in sq cm?' keys 12, and seed 45 'A square has a side of 5 m. What is its area in sq m?' keys 25. In every one of those the keyed answer is the product of the two given side lengths, never a perimeter or a side, so the samples do the finding the competency sentence asks for.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: All four cells of shape by unit that the wording names are present: square in sq cm at seed 502 'A square has a side of 4 cm. What is its area in sq cm?' (16), square in sq m at seed 45 (25), rectangle in sq cm at seed 604 'A rectangle has sides 8 cm and 5 cm. What is its area in sq cm?' (40), and rectangle in sq m at seed 606 'A rectangle has sides 4 m and 7 m. What is its area in sq m?' (28). Neither shape is confined to one unit, and the square cases include both the equal-sides-stated form and the single-side form.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Each area item is a single step over two one-digit lengths that are handed to the pupil explicitly: seed 605 'A rectangle has sides 5 cm and 6 cm. What is its area in sq cm?' needs only 5x6, and seed 44 'A square has a side of 3 cm. What is its area in sq cm?' needs the extra step of realising the second side is also 3. No item mixes cm and m inside one stem or demands a unit conversion, which suits a first formal exposure to area in Grade 3 Quarter 1.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Apart from seed 601 the packet runs on exactly two frozen sentence frames, and some samples repeat outright. Seed 50 and seed 500 are word-for-word 'A square has a side of 4 m. What is its area in sq m?' with the same distractor set 8, 15, 17; seed 502 is that same item with cm substituted; seed 42 'A rectangle has sides 4 cm and 3 cm' and seed 602 'A rectangle has sides 4 m and 3 m' likewise differ only by the unit; seed 44 and seed 501 are the 3 cm and 3 m versions of one square. No sample names a person, an object or a diagram, and the cloze renderings at seeds 50, 500 and 605 present the same four keyed choices as the mcq ones, so the formatter split adds no structural difference.

competency_alignment.rationale: Seed 601 does not ask for an area in square centimetres or square metres at all: 'Pia wants to cover a rectangular garden that is 5 cm long and 2 cm wide with square tiles. How many tiles are needed to cover it completely?' The keyed answer 10 is a count of tiles whose size is never stated, and the item is an applied tiling task of the sort the neighbouring problem-solving competency owns rather than a direct area calculation named in square units. The other thirteen samples all state the unit in the stem and belong squarely to this node.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Side lengths run from 2 to 8 and the keyed areas run from 9 at seed 44 (3x3) to 40 at seed 604 'A rectangle has sides 8 cm and 5 cm' (8x5). Every answer is therefore a multiplication fact inside the tables available in Grade 3 Quarter 1; the largest square is seed 45 'A square has a side of 5 m' at 25, and no item requires a two-digit factor or a two-digit by one-digit product.
